land.text: Tenochtitlan became the senior partner of the Triple Alliance

successors.note: Infobox 'Formation of the Aztec Empire: 1428' (Tenochtitlan page); the Tepanec War page has the treaty of the three cities in 1430.

capitals.name: Tenochtitlan (Mexico City)
capitals.note: The city itself is the polity; coordinates from the gazetteer's Mexico City. Tlatelolco, the 'sister city' founded to its north in 1337, was a separate altepetl until 1473.

correction.text: The island city in Lake Texcoco and its lake shore: 'Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325, but other researchers and anthropologists believe the year to be 1345'; 'Tenochtitlan covered an estimated 8 to 13.5 km2' (at its peak)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's shape (2,381 km2, 98.93-98.40 W, 18.86-19.57 N) begins in 1326, not 1325, and lies east of the city: its eight cells hold Texcoco and Coatlinchan but not the cell of Mexico City (the gazetteer finds none of the three Valley shapes contain it). Corrected to a 15 km disc at the city; the city's own area of 8 to 13.5 km2 (page, for the 16th-century peak) is far below the shape (factor of two exceeded, 175 times), and the polity's domain before 1428 is not on the pages. Years 1325-1421.

correction.text: The same island city and lake shore as for 1326-1421; 'Under Itzcoatl, the Mexica of Tenochtitlan broke free from Tepanec domination' (Itzcoatl page)

keyframe_review.note: 1422-1428, the same 2,381 km2 shape as 1326-1421, misplaced in the same way. The Mexica were under Tepanec domination until the war of 1427-1428 (Itzcoatl page); Cliopatria's split at 1422 has no event on the pages read.

region.text: the island in Lake Texcoco; 'the date 13 March 1325 was chosen in 1925 to celebrate the 600th anniversary of the city'

ledger.note: 1325: the Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco. Infobox 'Foundation: 1325'; 'The exact date of the founding of the city is unclear'; the Mexica page adds that 'other researchers and anthropologists believe the year to be 1345'. Cliopatria starts the shape in 1326.

1337: a dissident Mexica group founds Tlatelolco north of Tenochtitlan. 'A dissident group of Mexica separated from the main body and built another city on an island north of Tenochtitlan in 1337.' Tlatelolco stayed independent until Axayacatl's war of 1473 (Tenochtitlan page).

1427: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan and Huexotzinco go to war against Azcapotzalco. 'In 1427, Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan, and Huexotzinco went to war against Azcapotzalco, emerging victorious in 1428.' Itzcoatl (1427-1440) led the Mexica; the page names no battle.
1428: the allies win and the Tepanec lands are carved up. 'emerging victorious in 1428'; 'The Tepanec lands were carved up among the three cities'.
1428: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan found the Triple Alliance. Infobox 'Formation of the Aztec Empire: 1428'. The treaty is dated 1430 on the Tepanec War page.

region.text: the altepetl, continued in the Triple Alliance

ledger.note: 1428: the independent altepetl of Tenochtitlan ends as it becomes the head of the Aztec Triple Alliance (the city itself continues as the empire's capital to 1521).

wars.name: Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Azcapotzalco defeated in 1428; its lands carved up among Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, who formed the Triple Alliance.
wars.note: Tezozomoc died in 1426; Maxtla usurped the throne; Chimalpopoca of Tenochtitlan 'died shortly thereafter, possibly assassinated by Maxtla'. The page redirects to the Aztec Empire article and gives no battle.

certainty.note: An island city-state in a lake; its domain before 1428 is not described on the pages, and no border is known.

sources.title: Tenochtitlan

notes: Four pages (budget 1-2; two of them are the Aztec Empire and Itzcoatl pages opened for the Triple Alliance). (1) CLIOPATRIA SHAPE: the 2,381 km2 shape, 98.93-98.40 W, does not contain Tenochtitlan (99.13 W): its cells are the east of the Basin (Texcoco, Coatlinchan) and Cliopatria's Texcoco shape of 1326-1428 lies to the south (Xochimilco, Chalco); the two altepetl appear displaced. Both are corrected to discs at the cities. (2) START 1325 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1326; the Mexica page says 1325 or 1345. (3) NO TEPANEC VASSALAGE EVENT: the pages say only that the Mexica 'broke free from Tepanec domination' under Itzcoatl (no start year); the vassal relation belongs to the azcapotzalco dossier. (4) NO RULER LIST: Acamapichtli, Huitzilihuitl and Chimalpopoca are not on the pages read (the Tenochtitlan article does not cover rulers). (5) Pages Tenochtitlan and Aztec Empire say nothing on the altepetl's domain before 1428; the dossier draws only the city and its lake shore. (6) Tlatelolco (1337-1473) has no dossier.
